mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate below 0.1% indicates accommodative monetary policy, reducing discount rates for equity valuation and generating positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS remains below 0.1% for 3 consecutive months but S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of such periods.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in unemployment rate below 5.0% signals labor market tightening, boosting corporate earnings and producing positive S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: UNRATE falls below 5.0% but S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in consumer spending (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) indicates robust demand, driving corporate revenue and positive S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: RSAFS and HOUST both rise but S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of such periods.

mechanism_narrative: High inflation (CPIAUCSL > 2.5%) combined with declining industrial production (INDPRO) signals supply shocks reducing corporate output, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL > 2.5% and INDPRO falls, S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Rising inflation (CPIAUCSL) signals potential future monetary tightening, compressing equity valuations and leading to negative S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL rises but S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of such periods.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly payroll employment increase exceeding 100,000 persons indicates labor market strength, supporting consumer spending and generating positive S&P 500 returns in 5 trading days.
failure_condition: PAYEMS increases > 100,000 but S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of such periods.

mechanism_narrative: Strong GDP growth (GDPC1 > 16000) combined with moderate inflation (CPIAUCSL < 3.0%) signals a healthy economy, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: When GDPC1 > 16000 and CPIAUCSL < 3.0, S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In a high unemployment regime (UNRATE > 6.0%), a decline in unemployment signals labor market recovery, boosting corporate earnings and producing positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When UNRATE > 6.0% and UNRATE declines, S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of cases.
